The same 1.09 wave hit other 'god' uniques including Harlequin Crest (Shako) and Wizardspike.

veteranBlindspot: Younger D2R veterans dismiss Arkaine's as a leveling armor and don't know it was once a duped, top-of-the-economy item — the collapse is invisible unless you played 1.07-1.08.

collectorCase: This is a Pillar-2 historic pick. name: Corrupted item — high-rarity / +skills corruption (Project Diablo 2)
quality: Any (corrupted)
rarityTier: Rare best-case outcome on a 25%-brick gamble
priceSignal: Real demand, but inside the Project Diablo 2 (mod) economy, not official D2R. A godly base that lands a top corruption (for example +1 all skills, +2 to a class's skills, or Cannot Be Frozen) becomes best-in-slot and chase-priced; a bricked one is near-worthless. collectorCase: This is the honest answer to the 'corrupted items' request. Item corruption does NOT exist in official Diablo II: Resurrected. It is a mod mechanic, most famously in Project Diablo 2 (and the 'D2R Corruptions' D2RMM/Nexus mod). Its collector story is folklore-grade: a Worldstone Shard gamble can brick your best item or elevate it to best-in-slot. The all-or-nothing risk on an already-perfect base, and the legendary 'insane corruption' clips built around it, are exactly the museum-of-modded-D2 exhibit.
whyValuable: The top-tier corruption modifiers are generally stronger than the alternative sockets, so a well-corrupted item is straight best-in-slot in PD2. Because 1 in 4 attempts destroys the item, surviving godly corruptions are prestige pieces.
teachingPoint: In PD2 you corrupt by placing a Worldstone Shard with an item in the Horadric Cube. Outcomes: add sockets, add a corruption modifier, or brick (reroll into a random rare) at ~25%. Using a Puzzlebox first raises the modifier chance to 75%, but the 25% brick risk stays.
veteranBlindspot: An official-D2R veteran may assume corruption is a base-game feature (it is not) or may not play PD2 at all, so the entire mechanic and its economy are a blind spot. Flag clearly on the site so no one mistakes it for vanilla D2R.
history: Popularized by Project Diablo 2's seasonal ladders; the 'corrupt my best items' video genre made specific outcomes (D-Web, Templar's Might, +skill chests) into community legends.
factClaims: Official Diablo II: Resurrected has no item corruption; it is a mod feature (Project Diablo 2, and the D2RMM 'D2R Corruptions' mod).

In single-player / offline, selling a single SOJ on Hell difficulty triggers the 'Diablo Walks the Earth' message and lets you fight Uber Diablo.
Uber Diablo drops the Annihilus 100% of the time.

Blizzard's explicit intent as an anti-dupe sink is community inference, not a documented Blizzard statement.

name: Annihilus
quality: Roll-dependent. 10/10/5 is a low roll, 20/20/10 is perfect and the value jump is large.
rarityTier: Only unique small charm in the game; single-source drop
priceSignal: Steady high demand in D2R ladder. Per diablo2.io trade guides, low rolls (about 10/10/5) trade around Lo to Sur, mid rolls (14/14/7) around Sur to Ber, high rolls (18/18/9) around Ber to Jah, and near-perfect 20/20/10 for Jah and up. collectorCase: It is the prize the entire SOJ-sink mechanic exists to produce, and the only unique small charm ever made. whyValuable: A small charm that gives +1 all skills, +10-20 to every attribute, +10-20 all resistances and bonus experience is pure profit for any build, using only one inventory square. That universal value is why it anchors so much of the endgame trade.
history: Introduced with the 1.10 World Event as Uber Diablo's guaranteed drop. It is the reward half of the SOJ sink: the thing that made players want the event to fire. It also introduced the idea of a permanent character-power charm gated behind a server-wide, community-driven event.
veteranBlindspot: Veterans know Anni is great, but many underweight how sharp the roll curve is. A 20/20/10 is worth multiples of a 15/15/7, and players routinely undervalue a near-perfect one when trading fast.
teachingPoint: The Annihilus is the economic mirror of the SOJ. One item was the inflation problem, the other is the deflationary carrot the developers attached to the fix.
factClaims: Annihilus is the only unique small charm in Diablo 2.

name: Ber Rune

rarityTier: High rune (Mal-to-Zod bracket); common benchmark trade unit
priceSignal: Consistently one of the most-quoted currency units in D2R. Big-ticket uniques and runewords are routinely priced 'in Bers' on d2jsp and diablo2.io. Demand is structural because three of the best runewords need it. It holds value across a season better than almost anything.
collectorCase: Ber is the artifact of D2's currency succession. The SOJ story only closes when you show what replaced it. Ber earns its slot because it explains WHY the high-rune standard exists: damage-reduction stacking and the runeword demand curve, not raw rune rarity alone.
whyValuable: 8% Damage Reduced in armor is a coveted defensive mod, and Ber is a required rune in Enigma, Infinity (twice) and Chains of Honor. That built-in consumption keeps demand high and gives it currency-grade liquidity.
history: When patch 1.10 turned runewords into the endgame, demand for high runes exploded and the Mal-to-Zod bracket displaced the SOJ as the currency of Battle.net. In mature D2R ladder, the high-rune standard is the norm, and Ber is one of the common quoted units, the same liquidity role the SOJ once held.
veteranBlindspot: Everyone knows Ber is currency. Fewer articulate why Ber specifically became a pricing anchor rather than a rarer rune like Zod: it is the one high rune that is both defensively best-in-class (DR stacking to the cap) and burned by the most-wanted runewords, so it is always in motion.
teachingPoint: Currency in D2 is whatever is simultaneously liquid, universally demanded, and constantly consumed. The SOJ had it, then runewords handed that role to high runes.
factClaims: Ber is a high rune, part of the Mal-to-Zod high-rune bracket.
Socketed in body armor, helm or shield, Ber grants Damage Reduced by 8%.
Ber is required by Enigma (Jah Ith Ber), Infinity (Ber Mal Ber Ist, which uses two Bers), and Chains of Honor (Dol Um Ber Ist).
High runes replaced the Stone of Jordan as Diablo 2's trade currency after patch 1.10 made runewords the endgame.
In D2R's mature economy, high-value items are routinely priced in high runes, with Ber a common benchmark unit.

name: Enigma
quality: Best on a low-strength-requirement base like Mage Plate or Archon Plate; roll matters little.
rarityTier: High-cost runeword (needs Jah and Ber)
priceSignal: Among the most expensive and most demanded runewords in the game across every D2R ladder. Jah plus Ber makes it a high-rune purchase on any trade site. Demand is universal because every class wants one.
collectorCase: Listed here for IMPACT, not to explain what it does. Enigma is the single most economy-shaping runeword ever added. It universalized teleport, a skill that had been Sorceress-only, and in doing so it reset how every class moves, farms and fights. Its Jah and Ber cost also set a permanent price floor under two high runes and became a documented driver of rune duping.
whyValuable: Teleport on any class collapses travel time and farming speed for every build, and the strength-per-level bonus frees huge stat investment into vitality. That is why it is a near-mandatory chase piece.
history: Released in 1.10. Before Enigma, teleport belonged to the Sorceress. After it, any class with the runes moved like one. This reshaped PvP, boss rushing and MF farming simultaneously and permanently bent high-rune demand upward.
veteranBlindspot: The obvious pick, and veterans wave it off as 'just the teleport armor.' The under-appreciated part is economic: Enigma, more than any single item, is why Jah and Ber have the value they do and why rune duping was so lucrative.
teachingPoint: A single item can rewrite class design boundaries. Teleport stopped being a class identity and became a gear check the moment Enigma shipped.
factClaims: Enigma is the runeword Jah + Ith + Ber in a 3-socket body armor, available from patch 1.10.

It grants +2 to All Skills and +1 to Teleport to any class, +45% Faster Run/Walk, large defense scaling with level, +0.75 defense per level, +0-74 to Strength based on character level, and Damage Reduced by 8%.
Teleport was a Sorceress-only skill before Enigma made it available to every class via gear.
It is one of the most expensive runewords because it requires both Jah and Ber.

name: Hellfire Torch
quality: Class + roll dependent. Fixed +3 to a random class, plus 10-20 stats / 10-20 resist. A 20/20 of a wanted class is the trophy.
rarityTier: Only unique large charm; drops only from the Pandemonium Event
priceSignal: High demand in D2R ladder. Per diablo2.io guides, low rolls trade around a low high-rune, and a perfect 20/20 of a desirable class trades for Jah or higher in ladder. collectorCase: The Torch is the object that created an entire endgame economy from nothing. It is the only unique large charm, it comes only from a multi-step event, and its class-plus-roll matrix makes a perfect one of the right class a real collector target. The keys and organs feeding it became tradeable commodities in their own right.
whyValuable: +3 to a class's whole skill tree on a charm, plus up to +20 stats and +20 all resistances, is power no other charm approaches. The event gate keeps supply constrained.
history: Added in patch 1.11 with the Pandemonium Event (Uber Tristram). To earn a Torch you farm three each of the Key of Terror (Countess), Key of Hate (Summoner) and Key of Destruction (Nihlathak) on Hell, open three mini-uber portals for three organs, combine the organs to open Uber Tristram, then kill Uber Mephisto, Uber Baal and Pandemonium Diablo. This spawned a durable market in keys, organ sets and torch-rolling.
veteranBlindspot: Veterans track Anni closely but often sleep on Torch class-rolls. A 20/20 Torch of a meta class is rarer and can be worth more than a comparable Anni, and off-class torches are dramatically cheaper than on-class ones.
teachingPoint: The Pandemonium Event shows how a single reward item can bootstrap a whole sub-economy of intermediate goods (keys and organs) that trade independently of the final prize.
factClaims: Hellfire Torch is the only unique large charm in Diablo 2.

It is obtained only from the Pandemonium Event / Uber Tristram, added in patch 1.11.

name: Grief
alias: Eth Tir Lo Mal Ral (Phase Blade)
quality: Base-dependent. A perfect-roll Grief in an eth Phase Blade or eth Berserker Axe carries a real premium over a plain one.
rarityTier: Mid-high cost runeword; the defining melee weapon since 1.10
priceSignal: Permanent staple demand in D2R. A rolled Grief Phase Blade is a standard purchase, and a high-damage roll (near +400) on a top base commands a premium on d2jsp and diablo2.io. It never falls out of demand because it is best-in-slot for most physical melee.
collectorCase: Grief is the item that ended a debate. From 1.10 on it is so far ahead of every other melee weapon that it defines the entire physical-melee meta, and its +340-400 flat damage mod behaves unlike any other stat in the game. A perfect-roll Grief on a perfect base is a collector piece precisely because the ceiling is so sought after.
whyValuable: The flat +340-400 damage acts like raw weapon damage, so it scales hardest on the fastest, lowest-base-damage weapons. On a naturally indestructible Phase Blade with the game's fastest base speed, the result is absurd single-hit output plus ignore-defense and prevent-monster-heal utility.
history: Released in 1.10. It reshaped melee build theory overnight and made most unique and set melee weapons obsolete for serious play. It is routinely called the best melee weapon in the game, sometimes 'so good it is broken.'
veteranBlindspot: Even veterans misremember the damage as a percentage boost. It is a flat add, which is exactly why it wrecks fast low-damage weapons and why Phase Blade, not a big two-hander, is the iconic base.
teachingPoint: Grief teaches how a single non-standard damage mechanic (flat added damage that reads like base weapon damage) can invert normal weapon-balance logic and pick winners among bases the designers never intended.
factClaims: Grief is the runeword Eth + Tir + Lo + Mal + Ral in a 5-socket Sword or Axe, available from patch 1.10.
Its signature mod is +340-400 Damage, a flat damage add that functions like added weapon damage.

Other mods include 35% chance to cast Level 15 Venom on striking, +30-40% Increased Attack Speed, Ignore Target's Defense, -25% Target Defense, 20% Deadly Strike, Prevent Monster Heal, damage to demons per level, +2 Mana after each kill, and +10-15 Life after each kill.
The Phase Blade is a favored base because it has the fastest base attack speed in the game and is naturally indestructible.
It is widely regarded as the best melee weapon in Diablo 2.

name: Infinity
quality: Best on an ethereal Giant Thresher or Great Poleaxe for the mercenary. Conviction rolls to level 12.
rarityTier: High-cost runeword (two Ber runes)
priceSignal: Expensive and in constant demand in D2R because it needs two Ber runes. An eth-base Infinity is a major purchase on any trade site. Demand is propped up by how many farming builds it enables.
collectorCase: Infinity is here for what it unlocked, not its raw damage. Its Level 12 Conviction aura on a mercenary broke the immunity wall that had capped lightning builds for years. It turned Lightning Sorceress, Javazon and Lightning Trapsin from immunity-blocked novelties into premier farmers and redefined what a mercenary weapon is for.
whyValuable: The aura lowers enemy resistances and defense in a wide radius, breaking most single elemental immunities and multiplying elemental damage. On an Act 2 merc it benefits the whole party passively, which is why it is best-in-slot support gear.
history: Released in 1.10. Before Infinity, lightning builds were throttled by lightning-immune monsters they could not break. Putting Conviction on a merc weapon changed which builds were viable in the farming meta and shifted the mercenary from a bodyguard into an aura battery.
veteranBlindspot: Many treat it as 'the lightning sorc merc weapon' and stop there. The broader point is that it retroactively rescued several entire build archetypes from immunity-lockout, which is a meta shift, not just a gear upgrade.
teachingPoint: Infinity shows that support items can be more meta-defining than damage items. Enabling a build to exist at all is a bigger economic event than making an existing build hit harder.
factClaims: Infinity is the runeword Ber + Mal + Ber + Ist in a 4-socket polearm or spear, available from patch 1.10.
It provides a Level 12 Conviction aura when equipped.
It carries -(45-55)% to Enemy Lightning Resistance, plus chance to cast Chain Lightning and Crushing Blow.
It requires two Ber runes, making it one of the costlier runewords.
It is the standard mercenary weapon for enabling lightning-based builds against immunities.

name: Wirt's Leg
quality: All copies are identical. There is no good or bad roll.
rarityTier: Trivially obtained; historically priceless, monetarily worthless
priceSignal: No trade value. Every character can grab one for free in Tristram. This is the deliberate F-tier inclusion: it has essentially zero market demand, and it earns its slot purely on historic significance, which is exactly the kind of split the site should teach.
collectorCase: It is the physical key to Diablo 2's most famous secret, and a direct callback to a Diablo 1 community myth that Blizzard made real. As a museum object it represents the studio turning a fan rumor into canon. You cannot own a 'better' one, so the value is entirely story.
whyValuable: Its only function is combat-irrelevant: combine it with a Tome of Town Portal in the Cube to open the Secret Cow Level, one of the game's core farming and leveling runs.
history: In Diablo 1 a persistent rumor claimed clicking a cow enough times opened a secret cow level. It was a myth. Diablo: Hellfire winked at it with the Jersey's Jersey quest, and Diablo 2 finally made the Secret Cow Level real, opened with Wirt's Leg plus a Tome of Town Portal. In original D2/LoD, being present when the Cow King died locked you out of opening the portal yourself on that difficulty. D2R removed that restriction.
veteranBlindspot: Veterans know the recipe cold, but many have forgotten that the whole level is a monument to a Diablo 1 hoax, and that the old Cow King lockout rule (which shaped how groups ran cows for years) is gone in D2R.
teachingPoint: Not every historically significant item has market value. Wirt's Leg is the clean example of significance driven purely by folklore and design history.
factClaims: Wirt's Leg is obtained by clicking Wirt's corpse in Tristram in Act 1.
Combining Wirt's Leg with a Tome of Town Portal in the Horadric Cube, while in the Rogue Encampment and after completing the current difficulty, opens the portal to the Secret Cow Level.
In original Diablo 2 / LoD, a character present when the Cow King was killed could no longer open the Cow portal on that difficulty; D2R removed this restriction.
The Secret Cow Level was Blizzard's realization of a Diablo 1 fan rumor that had been a myth in that game.

name: The Gull
alias: Gull Dagger, the duper's safety tool
quality: Fixed unique. Any copy is the same.
rarityTier: Cheap unique; the folklore is what is rare knowledge
priceSignal: Nearly worthless as an item in D2R. It is farmed as an early magic-find dagger and trades for pennies. It is on this list for a genuinely obscure historic reason, not for demand. If anything, its cheapness is the point.
collectorCase: This is the surprise pick for a veteran. A junk +100% magic-find dagger had a documented second life as a safety tool in Battle.net duplication methods. In the 'Staff in Orifice' dupe, one step incremented the character's mana and risked character corruption, and the Gull's -5 to Mana was equipped specifically to counteract that and keep the character from breaking. A throwaway treasure-hunting dagger became duper's equipment.
whyValuable: As a legitimate item, only its early-game magic find matters. Its historic interest is entirely the dupe-era folklore, which almost no seasoned player knows.
history: The Gull is a low-damage unique dagger prized early for magic find. Separately, community writeups of D2 dupe exploits document that its negative-mana property was used to prevent mana-overflow character corruption during specific duplication steps, making it a niche tool of the illegit economy.
veteranBlindspot: Ask a veteran about the Gull and you get 'early MF dagger, who cares.' Almost none know it was equipped as a corruption safeguard inside actual dupe procedures. That is the whole reason it belongs in a significance list.
teachingPoint: Item significance is not only about intended use. The Gull is proof that a stat the designers meant as a downside (-5 mana) became load-bearing in the game's underground economy.
factClaims: The Gull is a unique dagger with +100% Better Chance of Getting Magic Items and -5 to Mana, low damage, used early game for magic find.
Documented Diablo 2 duplication walkthroughs describe using the Gull's -5 mana to counteract a mana-increment step that risked character corruption during the exploit.
The Blade of Ali Baba only surpasses the Gull's magic find when socketed with Ist runes at higher character level.

name: The White Ring
quality: Illegit; stats were impossible combinations.
rarityTier: Removed hacked item; does not exist in D2R
priceSignal: No legitimate market and not obtainable in D2R at all. On old Battle.net it was traded as a hacked collectible among a small circle who knew of it. Its value is pure folklore, and it must be framed as illegit, never as something a player can chase.
collectorCase: The White Ring is the emblem of D2's hacked-item era. It came out of open Battle.net where items could be built with no requirements and impossible stat combinations, then circulated on closed Battle.net as a legend most players had never even seen. It represents the whole category of illegit items (08s, Iths, Whites, bugged eth Zods) that pushed Blizzard toward dupe and impossible-item detection.
whyValuable: It has no legitimate value. Its worth is entirely as collector folklore and as a marker of the exploit era that shaped Blizzard's anti-dupe response.
history: Hacked and bugged items proliferated on closed Battle.net roughly between the 1.08 and 1.10 patches. The White Ring, an impossible-stat ring originating from open Battle.net, was popular in that window and is cited as no longer existing by v1.14d. The broader wave of illegit items is credited with prompting dupe and impossible-item scanners.
veteranBlindspot: Plenty of long-time players have literally never heard of the White Ring, which is unusual for something so storied. That obscurity is the point: it lived in a small hacked-item subculture, not the mainstream economy.
teachingPoint: Illegit items are part of the historical record. The White Ring shows how the exploit economy forced real design responses (detection and removal), the same way SOJ duping forced the World Event.
factClaims: The White Ring is a hacked/illegit ring, not a legitimately dropable item.
It originated from open Battle.net, where items could be created with no requirements and impossible stat combinations, and circulated on closed Battle.net.
It is described as no longer existing as of patch 1.14d and is not present in D2R.
It belongs to the same illegit-item era as 08 uniques, Ith-bugged items and bugged ethereal Zod items.

name: The Grandfather (pre-1.10, one-handed)
quality: Legacy version. The value is in the old classification and old stat set, which cannot roll today.
rarityTier: Legacy / non-ladder collector; cannot exist in D2R
priceSignal: On original Diablo 2 legacy non-ladder realms, pre-1.10 items are prized collector goods that survive only through trade, since they can no longer drop. In D2R this version does not exist at all, so it is a pure collector artifact, not a live-economy item. Frame the demand as museum-tier among legacy collectors, not as a D2R purchase.
collectorCase: The Grandfather is the clean example of a patch reclassification creating a collector market. In Diablo 1 it was a lusted-after one-handed great sword, and that carried into D2 through patch 1.09, where it was a premier Barbarian weapon. Patch 1.10 made it two-handed and reworked its stats, so the old one-handed version froze in time. Surviving pre-1.10 copies are legacy trophies.
whyValuable: Historically the appeal was a top-tier sword you could use one-handed (with a shield or in a dual setup), plus an older stat block including percentage max life and mana and bonus strength and dexterity that the modern version lost. Today the value is collector scarcity, not build power.
history: Diablo 1 treated the Grandfather as a coveted one-handed great sword. In D2 through 1.09 it kept a one-handed profile and a stronger legacy stat set (in 1.08 it carried +20 Strength, +20 Dexterity, +25% max mana, +25% max life, +175 Life, +150% enhanced damage, +2.5 max damage per level, Indestructible). Patch 1.10 changed it to two-handed and reworked it, which killed its Barbarian appeal and created the legacy collectible.
veteranBlindspot: Younger D2R players know the Grandfather only as a heavy two-hander and are surprised it was once a prized one-handed weapon. Veterans who remember it often forget how different the 1.08/1.09 stat block was from today's.
teachingPoint: Nerfs and reclassifications create collector value by freezing a superseded version in place. The pre-1.10 Grandfather is the archetype of the legacy item that a patch, not rarity, made precious.
factClaims: In patches through 1.09 the Grandfather functioned as a one-handed sword and was a favored Barbarian weapon; patch 1.10 made it two-handed.

In patch 1.08 the Grandfather carried +20 Strength, +20 Dexterity, +25% to Maximum Mana, +25% to Maximum Life, +150% Attack Rating, +175 to Life, +2.5 max damage per character level, +150% Enhanced Damage, and Indestructible.
Pre-1.10 versions can no longer drop and survive only as legacy trade items on original Diablo 2 non-ladder realms.
The pre-1.10 one-handed version does not exist in Diablo 2 Resurrected, which uses the modern two-handed stats.

name: Zod Rune
quality: N/A.
rarityTier: Rarest rune in the game; commonly ranked the second-rarest item after Tyrael's Might
priceSignal: High value in D2R but with niche demand. It is the rarest rune, yet most builds rarely need one, so it trades as a premium collectible and a specialist tool for making ethereal gear permanent rather than as a bulk currency. Strong asking prices on d2jsp and diablo2.io, but thinner turnover than mid high runes.
collectorCase: Zod carries two museum hooks at once. It is the rarest naturally dropping rune and the only source of true Indestructible, and it sits at the center of a famous 1.09 ethereal bug. The eth-Zod story is real D2 lore: whether a Zod fixed or ruined an ethereal item depended on hidden durability rules, and that quirk fed the bugged-item collector scene.
whyValuable: Indestructible lets a character use an ethereal item forever, keeping the ethereal damage or defense bonus and lower requirements with no durability loss. That is the endgame use, and it is why an eth base plus Zod is a deliberate build choice.
history: Zod is the rarest rune and, by common community ranking, the second-rarest item after Tyrael's Might. In v1.09 an ethereal-Zod bug existed: a Zod placed in an ethereal item that had bonus durability could drop it to zero and ruin it, while a Zod in an ethereal item without bonus durability made it permanently indestructible. The bug was fixed in 1.10. The era's bugged eth-Zod items became collector oddities.
veteranBlindspot: Veterans know Zod is rare, but many misremember the old eth-Zod interaction and assume Zod always simply made eth items permanent. In 1.09 it could destroy the wrong ethereal item, which is why the bug is remembered at all.
teachingPoint: Rarity plus a signature bug is a strong significance combination. Zod is both the scarcest rune and a piece of patch-history folklore about how ethereal durability used to work.
factClaims: Zod is the rarest rune in Diablo 2 and is commonly ranked the second-rarest item overall, behind Tyrael's Might.
Socketing a Zod grants Indestructible and sets the item's required level to 69 if not already higher.
Its primary use is making ethereal items indestructible so their boosted stats and lower requirements can be used permanently.

In v1.09 an ethereal-Zod bug existed and was fixed in 1.10: a Zod in an ethereal item with bonus durability could ruin it, while a Zod in an ethereal item without bonus durability made it indestructible.
A Zod can be made in the Horadric Cube from 2 Cham runes plus a Flawless Emerald.

name: Tyrael's Might
quality: Roll matters for collectors (30/30 strength and resist is the top), but rarity dominates value.
rarityTier: Rarest item in the game
priceSignal: The classic 'rarest item' price paradox. On diablo2.io and d2jsp, high-roll copies are quoted around two Jah runes as a baseline, but interest is inconsistent because the armor has no +skills, so demand does not match its rarity. It is a trophy market: extreme scarcity, capped by mediocre build utility. That gap is the interesting part.
collectorCase: This is the grail. Tyrael's Might is the rarest item in Diablo 2, drops from an extremely limited pool of high-level monsters, and cannot spawn ethereal because it is Indestructible. It is prized almost purely as a trophy, which makes it the definitive museum piece: maximum rarity, deliberately modest build value.
whyValuable: It offers strong defense, damage to demons, faster run/walk, all resistances, cannot be frozen, and the useful 'Slain Monsters Rest in Peace' (which stops corpse-based enemy skills). But with no +skills, its price is driven by rarity and prestige, not power.
history: Because its base sits in treasure class 87, only very high-level monsters can drop the base at all, and even then it is roughly a 1-in-9 chance to be Tyrael's rather than another possible unique. Its Indestructible mod means a unique ethereal Sacred Armor is always Templar's Might, never Tyrael's. In D2R its Indestructible is noted as Ladder Only.
veteranBlindspot: Veterans assume the rarest item must be the most valuable. Tyrael's flips that: it is rarer than any high rune yet often trades for less than build-defining gear because it grants no skills. Rarity and price are not the same axis.
teachingPoint: Rarity does not equal demand. Tyrael's Might is the cleanest lesson on the wall: the scarcest object in the game is a trophy, priced by prestige rather than by how much it improves a character.
factClaims: Tyrael's Might is the rarest item in Diablo 2, a unique Sacred Armor.
Its base sits in treasure class 87, so only very high-level monsters can drop it, with roughly a 1-in-9 chance to be Tyrael's when a qualifying unique Sacred Armor drops.

Stats: 120-150% Enhanced Defense, +50-100% Damage to Demons, +20% Faster Run/Walk, +20-30 Strength, All Resistances +20-30, Requirements -100%, Cannot Be Frozen, Slain Monsters Rest in Peace, Indestructible. Required Level 84.
It cannot spawn ethereal because of its Indestructible mod, so a unique ethereal Sacred Armor is Templar's Might instead.
It has no +skills, which is why it is valued mainly as a collector trophy.
In Diablo 2 Resurrected its Indestructible property is listed as Ladder Only.
_domain: Diablo 2 / Diablo 2 Resurrected items with genuine historic significance (items that changed how the game was played or how its economy worked). Economy baseline: mature D2R ladder season. Audience: seasoned players.
